name: HUD Fair Market Rents (FMR)
coverage: national, every county/metro FMR area including small and rural markets Zillow doesn't cover
update_frequency: annual (effective each federal fiscal year, Oct 1)
history: yearly files published for many past fiscal years on huduser.gov
license: US Government (HUD) public domain data, free yearly files with no signup per secondary sources. A newer official API (noted by HUD's Office of Policy Development and Research) requires a free registration token for programmatic/current-year pulls; bulk yearly files don't need one.
cost: Free for the bulk yearly files; free token registration for the API.

correlation.notes: Not run — app/research/evaluate_series.py doesn't exist yet. Even without it, the structural mismatch below is a strong enough signal on its own.

potential_use: backend/app/scoring/neighborhood.py 'valuation' pillar's gross_rent_yield metric, currently fed by Zillow ZORI (ZIP-level, monthly). Would only add coverage in counties where Zillow has no ZORI series.
recommendation_summary: For NYC today this is strictly worse than what's already in use: annual cadence versus Zillow ZORI's monthly, county-level versus ZIP-level, and by design FMR targets the 40th percentile of gross rent for Section-8 payment standards rather than true market rent — mixing it into gross_rent_yield would introduce a systematic downward bias relative to the market-rate ZORI series already in production. Its only real use case is filling Zillow ZORI's rural/small-market coverage gaps once the area-model migration adds non-metro areas — worth a second look then, but not a fit for the app as it stands.
